purpose: OVERSEER. A third spec loop the operator asked for on 2026-09-07, after the first two completed: a system that connects to any AI harness, records what the agents are doing, and provides metrics and governance over them. New sibling project folder, spec loop inside it. This window proposes; it implements only the optional final skeleton, and only inside the new folder.
playbook: none -- one-off run. The queue below is the whole instruction. Round discipline is CLAUDE.md's.

queue.title: Spec loop R1 -- the overseer, in a new sibling folder
queue.detail: Read openspec/explorations/2026-09-07-an-overseer-for-any-harness.md FIRST. It is a seed: measurements to re-check, an honest assessment of the idea's risks, and questions you must ANSWER rather than inherit. Its central question is the one to settle before writing anything: is this a new product, or is it AgentWeave's Hub with the orchestration removed? The seed argues there IS a real distinction -- AgentWeave governs agents it spawns; an overseer governs agents it does not control -- but you must test that against the code rather than accept it. Your FIRST job is an inventory: what does AgentWeave already record, through what tables and what ingestion paths, and which of those are already reachable by a harness the Hub did not spawn. Then create the folder under C:\Users\huida\Documents\projects\, `git init` LOCALLY with no remote, scaffold openspec inside, and write the proposal there -- not in AgentWeave. Name the project yourself; 'overseer' is a working title, not a decision.
queue.result: witness created at C:/Users/huida/Documents/projects/witness (git init, no remote, commit 6b0a135). Inventory + proposal + design + tasks + 3 spec deltas; openspec validate --changes --strict passes. Framing settled AGAINST the seed's reason and FOR a stronger one: AgentWeave's security property is that identity is never accepted from a request, and an overseer's core operation is to accept a record about an actor it never authenticated. Measured: all 32 agent_actions routes gated on a run credential defined as a pointer into a runs row the Hub created; TurnUsage.run_id is a non-null unique FK with no HTTP writer, so cost is unreachable without a spawn; the 4 open ingestion routes require the INSTANCE-OPERATOR credential, not a project key (seed was wrong on both the paths and the auth model). Two seed corrections and two additions recorded: normalisation is NOT the gap (runner_parsing.py already does 3 harnesses), and the richest capture surface is the harness's own on-disk transcript, omitted from the seed's table -- 2,069 files / 985 MB on this machine, 17 record types, retroactive. Product commits to the passive lever and to no scoring; name carries the commitment. R1's own recommendation is propose-then-shelve pending 4 operator data-policy decisions.

queue.title: Spec loop R2 -- re-derive independently against AgentWeave's real recording layer
queue.detail: Not a re-read of R1. A fresh comparison against the code. For an extraction-adjacent proposal, R2's job is to compare it against THE THING IT DIFFERENTIATES FROM: read hub/hub/output_recording.py, the EventLog rows, the agent_outputs/runs/permission_requests/questions tables and the two compatibility self-report endpoints, and establish concretely how much of the proposed overseer AgentWeave already is. If the honest answer is 'most of it', say so -- that is a finding, not a failure, and it changes the proposal from a new product to a boundary question. Also check the seed's harness-capability table against anything in this repository that already parses or ingests a harness's output.
queue.result: witness at 3d75aaa. R1's three separation measurements re-derived independently and ALL THREE CONFIRMED (32 routes/32 get_agent_actor; TurnUsage.run_id unique non-null FK, 6 call sites in 2 non-route modules; both ingestion routes on Depends(get_project) under /projects/{project_id}). Everything else moved. Ran parse_claude_line unmodified over a real 2,070-line transcript rather than reading it: maps 2 of the file's 16 record types, 859 lines produce an event, 636 usage samples, 0 ACCOUNTING samples, session id on 1,337/2,070 because the file writes sessionId and the parser reads session_id, and the user branch emits only tool_results so the operator's PROMPT produces nothing (6 genuine prose prompts dropped). Verdict: the event vocabulary transfers, the parser does not, and the parts that transfer cleanly are the parts Witness needs least. THREE DEFECTS FIXED IN THE SPECS: (1) the capability matrix was keyed per-surface but reasoning text is present for haiku (398/421 blocks) and absent for opus-5 (0/1,987) and sonnet-5 (0/848) -- by MODEL, within one harness, on one surface, 625 vs 1,302 files with zero overlap -- so entries became always/never/conditional resolved per record; (2) no transcript in 2,095 files carries a `result` record and total_cost_usd is a JSON key in 0 files, so cost is UNOBSERVABLE on the only implemented surface while tokens are on 11,581/11,581 sampled assistant messages, so a fourth provenance state `derived` was added with measured-only inputs (AgentWeave's resolve_usage_limit is the precedent for why an undeclared derivation is unacceptable here); (3) a new requirement that the record carries the instruction. TWO R1 CLAIMS FALSIFIED: 'content is already there, complete and unredacted' is false for the two models the operator uses -- a completeness claim falsified by measurement inside the document proposing the fix; and 'nothing in AgentWeave targets Copilot' is wrong -- commit 1c6970d (2026-07-29) live-probed Copilot CLI 1.0.75, and its file exporter needs COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH set BEFORE SPAWN, so Copilot's file surface is neither passive nor retroactive; surfaces now declare both properties. T-2's plain question answered plainly: MOST of Witness already exists in AgentWeave's recording tables minus the FKs to runs; what is novel is the inverted identity requirement and the completeness statement. R2 also broke the proposal's own no-pasted-content rule in its first draft and left that recorded as evidence for OV-2. openspec validate --changes --strict passes.

queue.title: Spec loop R3 -- re-derive again, and confront the enforcement question
queue.detail: Third pass, because unlike the continuity kit this proposal has a large body of existing code to be wrong about. Its specific job: the seed's hardest question, which R1 and R2 will both be tempted to defer. Recording is passive; GOVERNING is active, and on a harness you do not control the only levers are a gateway that can refuse, a tool-boundary hook that can refuse, or an after-the-fact report. Those are three different products with three different deployment stories. Establish which one the proposal actually commits to and make it say so in design.md. Also test the proposal against this repository's own stated principle -- the unasked-question backstop was retired 2026-08-20 because guessing intent from prose is a judgement the product should not make on the operator's behalf. An overseer that scores or judges agent behaviour runs straight into it.
queue.result: witness at e2bb331. Assigned question settled and it needed a new decision: D3's 'after the fact' was covering two products, because the transcript is a LIVE append log -- a tool_use record readable on disk 0.114s and 0.202s after its own timestamp, by the command it describes. New D8: the first cut is a batch reader the operator runs, not a resident tailer; OV-1 does not authorise an unattended standing read, a forward-only tailer is the collector design D2 rejected, and the resident version's crash is silence indistinguishable from inactivity. Cost stated: no record outlives the harness's deletion window without something resident, so D8 and OV-3 are one decision (new OV-6). D4 tested AS WRITTEN and found to be intention rather than fence, twice: (1) completeness-report PERMITTED a per-agent completeness percentage -- over 14,701 assistant messages every fillable field is 100% on every model except reasoning text (haiku 407/1,022, opus 0/8,572, sonnet 0/5,094), so that figure ranks model choice on a page forbidding ranking; now per surface and per model, never per agent; (2) the 'operator writes the rules' sentence had no requirement behind it while the surface supplies 1,535 model-authored ai-title records to republish -- new author axis on every field, model-authored values counted apart and never reported, rules operator-only with none shipped and none model-evaluated. TWO MEASUREMENT CORRECTIONS: retroactivity has a floor -- 2,084 files/1.09GB spanning 2026-08-09 to today, 29 days, a cliff with zero files before it while >=51 earlier sessions are evidenced by committed handoffs, so 'retroactive' means to the HARNESS'S RETENTION WINDOW; and 169 delegated-agent transcripts sit at <session>/subagents/ carrying the PARENT's sessionId -- driven, keying on sessionId gives 1 actor with 545 turns, keying on the acting agent gives 9 with 370 turns (68%) delegated, so the requirement did not fail to prevent the misattribution, it prescribed it. R3 made the one-level-glob error itself first (1,915 vs 2,084). openspec validate --changes --strict passes.

decisions_for_user.question: May Witness read the local Claude Code transcript corpus at all?
decisions_for_user.evidence: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl is 2,069 files and 985 MB of your real sessions, containing prompts, source code, tool arguments and plausibly credentials, complete and unredacted. Unlike every OTel surface (where content is off until five flags are set), there is no vendor-side default withholding anything. It is also the ONLY surface that is retroactive -- it covers sessions that ran before the tool existed, which is all 2,069 of them. There is no partial answer that keeps the retroactive property. [R3] Two corrections to what is being asked: the corpus is 2,084 files / 1.09 GB counted recursively (R1's 2,069 and R2's 2,095 were one-level counts) and INCLUDES 169 delegated-agent transcripts under <session>/subagents/ that an operator picturing 'my sessions' would not picture; and the question is TIME-SENSITIVE, because the corpus deletes on a rolling window (oldest surviving file 2026-08-09, at least 51 earlier sessions already gone), so 'yes, later' is not the same answer as 'yes'.
decisions_for_user.blocks: Every phase of tasks.md except phase 0.

decisions_for_user.question: Redaction posture: at read, at write, or not at all?
decisions_for_user.evidence: At read loses fidelity permanently and makes the record less useful for the incident it was built for. At write leaves a window. Not at all makes the Witness store the most sensitive file on the machine. AgentWeave's redact_secrets (runner_events.py:63) is a working starting point either way.

decisions_for_user.question: Retention period for the record store.
decisions_for_user.evidence: A record that answers 'what did the agents do last quarter' must be kept for a quarter. That is a different risk profile from a debugging aid kept for a week. [R3] This is no longer only a risk-profile question: it determines the product's shape. A batch reader cannot keep a record past the harness's own deletion window; keeping more requires copying transcripts before deletion, which is a resident process. See OV-6.

decisions_for_user.question: Who may read the record -- you only, or anyone else?
decisions_for_user.evidence: Single-operator local is the first cut's assumption. The moment a second reader exists this becomes an access-control product and the scope roughly triples.

decisions_for_user.question: Does the name 'witness' survive?
decisions_for_user.evidence: Chosen because it commits the product to the passive posture -- a witness testifies to what it saw and is expected to say what it did not see. If a later round decides the product must enforce, the name must change too. Whether it collides with an existing project could not be checked offline.

decisions_for_user.question: Do you want a live mode, and would you run something resident to get it?
decisions_for_user.evidence: Measured this round: the Claude transcript is written live -- a record was readable on disk 0.114s and 0.202s after its own timestamp. A tailer is therefore buildable and design D8 deliberately does not build it, because a process reading your transcripts unattended is a larger disclosure than OV-1 asks about. It is also the ONLY way to keep records past the harness's deletion window (measured at 29 days with a hard cliff), so this and OV-3 are one decision wearing two hats: 'nothing resident' and 'records older than the window' cannot both be had.
decisions_for_user.blocks: design D8, and every task downstream of it if the answer is yes.
